content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal observations to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words not including the sentence given).

modelEssay.title: Elderly People's Contributions to Society
modelEssay.content: With their valuable skills and experience, elderly people can continue to make significant contributions to society. In many cultures, the wisdom accumulated by the elderly is highly valued. They often serve as mentors, guiding the younger generation with their insights and advice. For instance, retired professionals can volunteer in schools, sharing their knowledge and inspiring students to pursue their dreams. Moreover, elderly individuals can contribute to community development by participating in local organizations, where their experience in problem-solving and conflict resolution is invaluable. Lastly, their contributions extend to the family unit, where they provide emotional support and maintain family traditions, fostering a sense of continuity and stability. In conclusion, the contributions of the elderly are multifaceted, enriching society in ways that are both tangible and intangible.

structureAnalysis.paragraph1: 引入段：引用题目给定的句子，引出老年人对社会的贡献这一主题
structureAnalysis.paragraph2: 展开段：具体说明老年人在不同领域（教育、社区、家庭）的贡献，并举例说明
structureAnalysis.paragraph3: 总结段：总结老年人贡献的多样性及其对社会发展的重要性

运用了具体例子来支撑论点，如'retired professionals can volunteer in schools'
逻辑清晰，过渡自然（For instance, Moreover, Lastly, In conclusion）
词汇丰富，避免重复（skills, experience, wisdom, contributions）

transcript.text: So, I've been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I'd like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 所以，我一直在想，今年夏天，与其像往常一样租度假屋，不如试试租一辆房车，多探索一些地方。

transcript.text: A camper van? You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 房车？你是说整个夏天都住在车里吗？

transcript.text: Yes, a camper van. And no, it's nothing like living out of a car. These are proper vans with full-sized beds to sleep in. Some even have kitchens. This way, we wouldn't have to be locked into one place during our holiday. We'd be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace. The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway. We'd probably save a lot of money as well.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 是的，一辆房车。不，它完全不像住在车里。这些是正规的货车，里面有全尺寸的床可以睡觉。有些甚至还有厨房。这样，我们在假期就不必局限于一个地方。我们能够访问更多地方，按照自己的节奏旅行。反正夏天大多数酒店和度假屋的价格都会飙升。我们可能也会省下不少钱。

transcript.text: I think my grandfather had a van like that. It doesn't sound that appealing to me.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我觉得我祖父以前有一辆那样的车。这对我来说听起来并不那么吸引人。

transcript.text: Today's camper vans are completely different. These days, they're equipped with all the modern comforts. I've seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you're stopped. This way, you can still use your computer or charge your phone. And most even have Wi-Fi, so if the weather's not great, you could stream videos.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 如今的房车完全不同。现在，它们配备了所有现代舒适设施。我见过不少有太阳能板的，可以在停车时提供电力。这样，你仍然可以使用电脑或给手机充电。而且大多数甚至还有Wi-Fi，所以如果天气不好，你可以流媒体看视频。

transcript.text: I'm warming up to the idea. Keep talking.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 我开始对这个想法感兴趣了。继续说。

transcript.text: Loads of people are committing to this trend full-time. Check it out online. Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary. Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 很多人都全职投入这种趋势。在网上查一下。很多人流媒体直播他们另类的生活方式，实际上还能赚取薪水。想象一下，拥有那种自由，可以去任何你想去的地方，在世界任何地方工作。

transcript.text: Okay. We can consider it. As long as the basic needs like toilets and showers are covered, I'm definitely in. Do you think there will be enough room for my mountain bike? What about food delivery? Will we be able to order to the van? Will there be enough space for the dog? We wouldn't want to leave him behind.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 好的。我们可以考虑一下。只要基本需求如厕所和淋浴有保障，我绝对愿意。你觉得我的山地自行车有足够的空间吗？食物外卖呢？我们能点送到房车吗？狗有足够的空间吗？我们不想把它丢下。

transcript.text: Slow down. Glad you're excited about it. Let's start by looking at what's available first.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 别急。很高兴你对此感到兴奋。我们先看看有什么可用的。

transcript.text: You wanted to see me?
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: Yes. I'll get straight to the point. Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped. You've been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you. But what really concerns me is your curtailed output. Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind. What's going on?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 是的，我就直说了。过去一个月左右，你的表现明显下滑。你最近几周迟到了好几次，这很不像你。但真正让我担心的是你的产出减少了。最近，你似乎总是落后一步。发生了什么事？

transcript.text: I'm sorry. I'm going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment. It's a personal matter, so if you don't mind, I much prefer we don't get into it. Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.

transcript.text: I'm not sure why. I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.
transcript.speaker: F

transcript.text: You shouldn't feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你不应该为请假感到不好意思，尤其是当你需要的时候。

transcript.text: I know. You're right. I'm sorry.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我知道。你说得对。我很抱歉。

transcript.text: Look, you've been with us almost five years, and I personally really value your proficiency at your job. It makes my job far easier. In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你看，你在这里工作了将近五年，我个人非常欣赏你工作的熟练程度。这让我的工作轻松很多。此外，我可以向你保证，管理层整体上也对你评价很高。

transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.text: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%. Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?

transcript.text: It'll be enough. I'm sure of it.

transcript.text: Okay, good. So this is what we're going to do. You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self. Then, in two months' time, we will catch up again to see how you are fairing.

transcript.text: Sounds good. Thank you for your understanding.

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 篇章1。

transcript.text: There are many factors that impact our health. These include our finances, our emotions, and the way we work. Education is one such factor. Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.
transcript.translation: 许多因素影响我们的健康。这些包括我们的财务状况、情绪以及工作方式。教育就是这样一个因素。研究表明，更高的教育水平可以带来更好的健康，甚至更长的寿命。

transcript.text: But what about the education of your partner? New research seeks to answer this question. Researchers use data from a longitudinal study. The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957. The surveys ended in 2011.
transcript.translation: 但你伴侣的教育呢？新研究试图回答这个问题。研究人员使用了一项纵向研究的数据。这些数据来自1957年首次对高中生进行的调查。调查于2011年结束。

transcript.text: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health. This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants' own education, social background, and health status before and after marriage.
transcript.translation: 团队发现，配偶教育水平较高的人倾向于报告更好的健康状况。即使在调整其他因素（如参与者自己的教育水平、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况）后，情况依然如此。

transcript.text: The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional, and financial resources. These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money.
transcript.translation: 作者们认为，高水平的教育提供了共享的社会、智力、情感和财务资源。这些包括诸如更高水平的情商、特定技能或知识，或更多的金钱。

transcript.text: The researchers concede that an individual's own level of education is clearly important for their health. But they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner's education.
transcript.translation: 研究人员承认，个人自身的教育水平对其健康显然很重要。但他们也主张，个人同样可以从伴侣的教育中获益。

transcript.text: It is noteworthy that the effects varied by gender. For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse's education than for men. The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study. Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men. The researchers' hypothesis is that this made the husband's resources more likely to have a shared impact.
transcript.translation: 值得注意的是，这种效应因性别而异。对女性来说，健康与配偶教育水平的相关性比男性更强。团队认为这可能与研究的时间段有关。该样本中的女性教育水平和职业成就均低于男性。研究人员的假设是，这使得丈夫的资源更可能产生共享影响。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 篇章2。

transcript.text: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods. This is a serious risk to human lives and property. So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
transcript.translation: 气候科学家预测，世界上许多地区将越来越容易遭受洪水。这对人类生命和财产构成严重威胁。因此，理解和准确预测洪水风险是全球易受洪水影响的城市面临的一个关键挑战。

transcript.text: In 2017, Derek Loftus of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King. It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides. He'll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model called Tide Watch.
transcript.translation: 2017年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的德里克·洛夫图斯启动了一个名为'捕获国王'的项目。它使用智能手机应用程序收集普通公民在涨潮期间的数据。他将利用这些数据来验证和改进他的数学洪水模型，称为'潮汐观察'。

transcript.text: Loftus' mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there. But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy. Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground.
transcript.translation: 洛夫图斯的使命是提前知道水会流向哪里。但收集必要的数据并足够快地处理这些信息以制作可用的预测绝非易事。准确的洪水预测需要对地面情况的了解。

transcript.text: By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements. But they still didn't have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.
transcript.translation: 到21世纪初，超级计算已足够先进，科学家能够将天气预报模型与这些测量数据整合。但他们仍然缺乏实时预测快速移动洪水的关键能力。

transcript.text: So, in 2017, Loftus and colleagues set up a group of 28 internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia. The new sensors relay rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute.
transcript.translation: 因此，2017年，洛夫图斯和同事们在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的洪水风险社区设置了一组28个互联网连接的水位传感器。这些新传感器将水位高度和运动的粗略测量数据传输到弗吉尼亚研究所的计算机。

transcript.text: Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them real time to the Institute. Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.

transcript.text: Now, it's become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree. But as current population survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them. This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time. What has actually caused this decline?
transcript.translation: 如今，讨论大学学位的价值已成为一种例行话题。但正如当前人口普查数据显示，与拥有大学学位的男性相比，没有大学学位的男性就业率大幅下降。这一下降始于20世纪60年代，并随时间推移日益严重。究竟是什么导致了这种下降？

transcript.text: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades and have come up with several theories. One popular theory is that it's a case of too low wages for jobs that don't require a degree. An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
transcript.translation: 经济学家们数十年来一直在努力确定这一下降的根源，并提出了几种理论。一种流行的理论是，对于不需要学位的工作，工资太低了。另一种理论是，过去不需要大学学位的工作比现在多。

transcript.text: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem. Let's look at that paper now.
transcript.translation: 美国国家经济研究局最近的一篇工作论文回顾了这些理论，并对问题的原因提出了额外的假设。现在让我们来看看这篇论文。

transcript.text: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages. As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren't as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs. While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can't be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven't changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
transcript.translation: 首先，研究人员考虑了工资问题。随着拥有大学学位和没有大学学位的人之间的工资差距扩大，经济学家提出，男性对从事一些不太赚钱的工作兴趣减弱。尽管论文作者认为这一解释有道理，但他们断言低工资不能是唯一因素，因为没有大学学位的男性的工资，经通货膨胀调整后，自20世纪60年代以来变化不大，这让人难以理解为什么越来越少的男性似乎愿意接受这些工资。

transcript.text: This leads to the second theory, that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past. Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, two-thirds of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
transcript.translation: 这引出了第二种理论，即今天比过去有更多工作需要大学学位。确实，这一理论似乎成立，因为在今天的美国，三分之二的工作由至少受过一些大学教育的工人担任。

transcript.text: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem. They identified two new potential explanations. The first, being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s. And the second, being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage. These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or, if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
transcript.translation: 然而，论文作者认为还有其他因素加剧了这一问题。他们提出了两个新的潜在解释。第一个是自20世纪60年代以来，没有大学学位的男性结婚率大幅下降。第二个是女性参与劳动力市场的增加与结婚率下降同时发生。这两个变化意味着男性可能没有家庭需要供养，或者如果有家庭，他们的妻子可能承担了更多养家责任，这两种情况都可能削弱工作的经济动机。

transcript.text: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn't complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
transcript.translation: 论文作者承认，关于这一主题的研究尚未完成，但他们认为自己的工作支持了大学教育的价值。

transcript.text: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.
transcript.translation: 尽管越来越多的人试图少吃肉，但一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续发展报告中发现，这一趋势正从厨房蔓延到衣柜。

transcript.text: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.
transcript.translation: 研究发现，在购买衣服前考虑的问题列表中，动物福利居首，42%的人表示这对他们很重要。

transcript.text: The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as vegan, meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
transcript.translation: 该团队的研究人员预测，明年将出现不含动物成分的鞋类收藏热潮，因为他们听到各年龄段的购物者表示，他们会购买标注为纯素的鞋履，这意味着这些产品在生产过程中未使用任何动物或动物部位。

transcript.text: As well as being on trend, and with a much better ring to it than synthetic leather, the vegan label does convey an important extra distinction.
transcript.translation: 除了符合潮流，而且比合成皮革听起来更好之外，纯素标签确实传达了一个重要的额外区别。

transcript.text: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal-free. That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together, for example, and the chemicals used for finishing them.
transcript.translation: 如果你将某物标注为纯素，那么整个产品都需要是不含动物成分的。这意味着需要检查诸如粘合鞋子的胶水，以及用于处理它们的化学品等。

transcript.text: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time. In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
transcript.translation: 在高端市场，一些世界知名的时尚设计师已经避免使用皮革和毛皮一段时间了。事实上，一些公司现在正在探索用蘑菇制成的皮革替代品和丝绸替代品。

transcript.text: The Animal Free Product Society says they've seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark. In 2018, there were 119. So far this year, it says, an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered. New products are being added daily.
transcript.translation: 动物无产品协会表示，他们看到注册了纯素商标的产品激增。2018年有119个。今年到目前为止，他们说，已有前所未有的1,956个产品注册。新产品每天都在增加。

transcript.text: There are fur coats that are vegan, plastic vegan belts, and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labelled vegan.
transcript.translation: 有纯素的毛皮外套、塑料纯素腰带，以及由树皮或天然橡胶制成的标注为纯素的鞋子。

transcript.text: These new products aren't coming at an extra cost to consumers, though. Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals. New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99 and the vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
transcript.translation: 然而，这些新产品并未给消费者带来额外成本。纯素靴子的价格与皮革原版相同。New Look，首批使用纯素商标的知名连锁店之一，将芭蕾鞋定价为7.99英镑，纯素笔记本电脑手提包定价为29.99英镑，与其其他产品相当。

transcript.text: This signifies a change. In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium.
transcript.translation: 这标志着一种变化。过去，道德产品，无论是公平贸易还是有机的，都价格较高。

transcript.text: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical. The debate over durability, crop growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials.
transcript.translation: 然而，尚不清楚这些新产品是否能被视为道德产品。关于耐久性、作物种植影响、污染和可回收性的争论是复杂的，更不用说围绕制造产品的人的工作条件的伦理问题，无论其成分材料是什么。

transcript.text: Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.
transcript.translation: 环保活动人士建议，最好的方法是少买，无论物品是由什么制成的。

transcript.text: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible and that the world was going to hell.
transcript.translation: 到2016年底，任何稍加关注新闻头条的人都极有可能得出结论，一切都很糟糕，世界正在走向地狱。

transcript.text: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses, or terror attacks.
transcript.translation: 世界各地的战争、致命病毒的传播或恐怖袭击很容易让人感到沮丧。

transcript.text: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
transcript.translation: 然而，2016年是人类历史上最好的一年。

transcript.text: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990, and 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
transcript.translation: 儿童死亡率大约是1990年的一半，每天有30万人获得电力供应。

transcript.text: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa, and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
transcript.translation: 美国、欧洲、亚洲、非洲以及全球整体的每一项物质和环境福利指标都有所改善，而非恶化。

transcript.text: We are living in history's most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
transcript.translation: 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时期，各类暴力都在急剧下降。

transcript.text: Those are the facts, so why aren't we all optimists?
transcript.translation: 这些是事实，那么为什么我们不都是乐观主义者呢？

transcript.text: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
transcript.translation: 在2015年YouGov的一项调查中，65%的英国人和81%的法国人表示他们认为世界正在变得更糟。

transcript.text: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
transcript.translation: 然而，根据众多合理的统计数据，这些人完全是错误的。

transcript.text: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century. Yet people do. Why?
transcript.translation: 任何理智的人都不应该希望生活在前几个世纪。然而人们却这样想。为什么？

transcript.text: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational. It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
transcript.translation: 我们普遍的绝望情绪是非理性的。它更多地反映了我们自己，而非事物的真实情况。

transcript.text: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors, but now, in a media-saturated era, constantly mislead us.
transcript.translation: 最好将其解释为各种心理偏见的结果，这些偏见对我们的进化祖先有其作用，但现在，在一个媒体饱和的时代，它们不断误导我们。

transcript.text: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong. This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
transcript.translation: 从前，担心一切可能出错的事情具有巨大的生存价值。这就是为什么坏新闻尤其引人注目。

transcript.text: In our evolutionary past, it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
transcript.translation: 在我们的进化过去，注意力容易被负面信息抓住是一件好事，因为它很可能预示着对我们自身生存的危险风险。

transcript.text: The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he'd be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
transcript.translation: 总是假设下一块岩石后面有狮子的穴居人通常会错，但他比总是假设相反情况的人更有可能生存和繁衍。

transcript.text: But that was all before newspapers, television, and the internet.
transcript.translation: 但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前的事了。

transcript.text: In today's hyper-connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe.
transcript.translation: 在当今高度互联的时代，我们对坏新闻的沉迷只会让我们从全球各地吸收令人沮丧或愤怒的故事。

transcript.text: Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are.
transcript.translation: 无论这些新闻故事是否威胁到我们，我们都得出结论，事情比实际情况要糟糕得多。

transcript.text: Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events, by definition, aren't news.
transcript.translation: 另一方面，真正的好消息在报纸上可能更难发现，因为可预测的日常事件，顾名思义，不是新闻。

Now it is clear that these improvements provide great benefits but also __26__ health costs. Recent studies show that urban __27__ encourages more driving and is associated with heavier weight. paragraphs.text: Unfortunately, urban planning still centers in large part on solving the problems of the past. Of course cities still need to __30__ standard public health practices, such as separating toxic facilities from homes and restricting heavy truck traffic through __31__ residential areas. But it's also important to create healthier cities—and the discussion is already underway. questionGroups.title: Can Learning a Foreign Language Prevent Dementia?

material.title: Can Learning a Foreign Language Prevent Dementia?

paragraphs.text: You may have heard that learning another language is one method for preventing or at least postponing the onset of dementia. Dementia refers to the loss of cognitive abilities, and one of its most common forms is Alzheimers disease (阿尔茨海默氏病). At this time, the causes of the disease are not well understood, and consequently, there are no proven steps that people can take to prevent it. Nonetheless, some researchers have suggested that learning a foreign language might help delay the onset of dementia.
paragraphs.translation: 你可能听说过，学习另一种语言是预防或至少推迟痴呆症发作的一种方法。痴呆症指的是认知能力的丧失，其最常见形式之一是阿尔茨海默病（阿尔茨海默氏病）。目前，该病的病因尚不明确，因此没有已证实的预防步骤。尽管如此，一些研究者认为学习外语可能有助于延迟痴呆症的发作。

paragraphs.text: To explore this possibility more deeply, let's look at some of the common misconceptions about dementia and the aging brain. First of all, dementia is not an inevitable part of the normal aging process. Most older adults do not develop Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia. It is also important to remember that dementia is not the same thing as normal forgetfulness. At any age, we might experience difficulty finding the exact word we want or have trouble remembering the name of the person we just met. People with dementia have more serious problems, like feeling confused or getting lost in a familiar place. Think of it this way: If you forget where you parked your car at the mall, that's normal; if you forget how to drive a car, that may be a signal that something more serious is going on.
paragraphs.translation: 为了更深入地探讨这种可能性，让我们看看关于痴呆症和衰老大脑的一些常见误解。首先，痴呆症不是正常衰老过程的必然部分。大多数老年人不会患上阿尔茨海默病或其他形式的痴呆症。同样重要的是要记住，痴呆症与正常的健忘不同。在任何年龄，我们都可能遇到找不到确切词汇或记不住刚见面的人的名字的困难。痴呆症患者有更严重的问题，比如感到困惑或在熟悉的地方迷路。这样想：如果你在购物中心忘记车停在哪里，那是正常的；如果你忘记如何开车，那可能是更严重问题的信号。

paragraphs.text: The idea that dementia can be prevented is based on the comparison of the brain to a muscle. When people talk about the brain, they sometimes say things like "It is important to exercise your brain" or "To stay mentally fit, you have to give your brain a workout." Although these are colorful analogies, in reality the brain is not a muscle. Unlike muscles, the brain is always active and works even during periods of rest and sleep. In addition, although some muscle cells have a lifespan of only a few days, brain cells last a lifetime. Not only that, but it has been shown that new brain cells are being created throughout one's lifespan.
paragraphs.translation: 痴呆症可以预防的想法基于将大脑比作肌肉。当人们谈论大脑时，他们有时会说“锻炼大脑很重要”或“为了保持心理健康，你必须让大脑锻炼”。尽管这些是生动的类比，但现实中大脑不是肌肉。与肌肉不同，大脑始终活跃，即使在休息和睡眠期间也在工作。此外，尽管一些肌肉细胞只有几天的寿命，但脑细胞持续一生。不仅如此，研究表明，在人的一生中，新的脑细胞一直在被创建。

paragraphs.text: While it makes for a colorful analogy, comparing the brain to a muscle is inaccurate and misleading. So, if the brain is not a muscle, can it still be exercised? Once again, researchers don't know for sure. There are now many computer, online, and mobile device applications that claim to be able to "train your brain," and they typically tap into a variety of cognitive abilities. However, research suggests that although this type of training may improve one's abilities at the tasks themselves, they don't seem to improve other abilities. In other words, practicing a letter-detection task will, over time, improve your letter-detection skills, but it will not necessarily enhance your other perceptual abilities.
paragraphs.translation: 虽然这是一个生动的类比，但将大脑比作肌肉是不准确和误导的。那么，如果大脑不是肌肉，它还能被锻炼吗？再次强调，研究人员尚不确定。现在有许多计算机、在线和移动设备应用程序声称能够“训练你的大脑”，它们通常涉及各种认知能力。然而，研究表明，尽管这种训练可能提高任务本身的能力，但似乎不能提高其他能力。换句话说，练习字母检测任务会随着时间的推移提高你的字母检测技能，但不一定能增强你的其他感知能力。

paragraphs.text: However, there is some reason to believe that learning languages might be different. The best evidence that foreign language learning confers cognitive benefits comes from research with those who are already bilingual (双语的). Bilingualism most commonly occurs when children are exposed to two languages, either in the home(mom speaks Dutch, dad speaks Spanish) or more formally in early schooling. But bilingualism certainly occurs in adulthood as well.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，有一些理由相信学习语言可能不同。外语学习能带来认知益处的最好证据来自对那些已经是双语者的研究。双语现象最常见于儿童在家庭中接触两种语言（母亲说荷兰语，父亲说西班牙语），或更正式地在早期学校教育中。但双语现象当然也发生在成年期。

paragraphs.text: Bilingualism and multilingualism are actually more common than you might think. In fact, it has been estimated that there are fewer monolingual speakers in the world than bilinguals and multilinguals. Although in many countries most inhabitants share just one language, other countries have several official languages. Switzerland, for example, has four official languages: German, French, Italian, and Romansh. Throughout large parts of Africa, Arabic, Swahili, French, and English are often known and used by individuals who speak a different, native language in their home than they do in the marketplace. So bilingualism and multilingualism are to be found throughout the world. And with regard to cognitive abilities, the research on those who speak more than one language paints an encouraging picture.
paragraphs.translation: 双语和多语现象实际上比你想象的更常见。事实上，据估计，世界上单语者比双语者和多语者少。尽管在许多国家，大多数居民只共享一种语言，但其他国家有几种官方语言。例如，瑞士有四种官方语言：德语、法语、意大利语和罗曼什语。在非洲的大部分地区，阿拉伯语、斯瓦希里语、法语和英语经常被那些在家说不同于市场的本地语言的人所了解和使用。因此，双语和多语现象在全世界都能找到。关于认知能力，对那些说多种语言的研究描绘了一幅令人鼓舞的图景。

paragraphs.text: For one thing, bilinguals are better at multitasking. One explanation of this superiority is that speakers of two languages are continually inhibiting one of their languages, and this process of inhibition confers general cognitive benefits to other activities. In fact, bilingual individuals outperform their monolingual counterparts on a variety of cognitive tasks, such as following complex instructions, and switching to new instructions. For the sake of completeness, it should be noted that the advantages of being bilingual are not universal across all cognitive domains. Bilingual individuals have been shown to have smaller vocabularies and to take longer in retrieving words from memory when compared to monolinguals. In the long run, however, the cognitive and linguistic advantages of being bilingual far outweigh these two drawbacks.
paragraphs.translation: 首先，双语者更擅长多任务处理。这种优越性的一种解释是，双语者持续抑制其中一种语言，而这种抑制过程为其他活动带来了普遍的认知益处。事实上，双语个体在各种认知任务上表现优于单语对手，如遵循复杂指令和切换到新指令。为了完整起见，应该注意双语的优势并非在所有认知领域都普遍。研究表明，与单语者相比，双语个体词汇量较小，从记忆中检索单词的时间更长。然而，从长远来看，双语的认知和语言优势远远超过这两个缺点。

paragraphs.text: If the benefits of being bilingual spill over to other aspects of cognition, then we would expect to see a lower incidence of Alzheimer's disease in bilinguals than in monolinguals, or at least a later onset of Alzheimer's for bilinguals. In fact, there is evidence to support this claim. The psychologist Ellen Bialystok and her colleagues obtained the histories of 184 individuals who had made use of a memory clinic in Toronto. For those who showed signs of dementia, the monolinguals in the sample had an average age of 71.4 years at time of onset. The bilinguals, in contrast, received their diagnosis at 75.5 years, on average. In a study of this sort, a difference of four years is highly significant, and could not be explained by other systematic differences between the two groups. For example, the monolinguals reported, on average, a year and a half more schooling than their bilingual counterparts, so the effect was clearly not due to formal education.
paragraphs.translation: 如果双语的优势溢出到认知的其他方面，那么我们期望看到双语者中阿尔茨海默病的发病率低于单语者，或者至少双语者的阿尔茨海默病发作较晚。事实上，有证据支持这一主张。心理学家Ellen Bialystok和她的同事获取了184位使用多伦多记忆诊所的个人历史。对于那些表现出痴呆症状的人，样本中的单语者在发病时的平均年龄为71.4岁。相比之下，双语者平均在75.5岁时得到诊断。在这种研究中，四年的差异具有高度显著性，不能用两组之间的其他系统差异来解释。例如，单语者报告的平均教育年限比双语对手多一年半，所以效果显然不是由于正规教育。

paragraphs.text: A separate study, conducted in India, found strikingly similar results: bilingual patients developed symptoms of dementia 4.5 years later than monolinguals, even after other potential factors, such as gender and occupation, were controlled for. In addition, researchers have reported other positive effects of bilingualism for cognitive abilities in later life, even when the person acquired the language in adulthood. Crucially, Bialystok suggested that the positive benefits of being bilingual were only found in those who used both languages all the time.
paragraphs.translation: 在印度进行的另一项研究发现了惊人的相似结果：双语患者比单语者晚4.5年出现痴呆症状，即使在控制了其他潜在因素如性别和职业之后。此外，研究人员报告了双语对晚年认知能力的其他积极影响，即使该语言是在成年期习得的。关键的是，Bialystok提出，双语的积极益处只在那些一直使用两种语言的人中发现。

paragraphs.text: But encouraging as these kinds of studies are, they still have not established exactly how or why differences between bilinguals and monolinguals exist. Because these studies looked back at the histories of people who were already bilingual, the results can only say that a difference between the two groups was found, but not why that difference occurred. Further research is needed to determine what caused the differences in age of onset between the two groups.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管这类研究令人鼓舞，但它们尚未确切确立双语者和单语者之间差异的存在方式或原因。因为这些研究回顾了已经是双语者的历史，结果只能说发现了两组之间的差异，但不能说为什么发生这种差异。需要进一步研究来确定导致两组之间发病年龄差异的原因。

paragraphs.text: Other studies of successful aging suggest that being connected to one's community and having plenty of social interaction is also important in delaying or even preventing the onset of dementia. Once again, however, the results are far less clear than the popular media might lead you to believe. Older individuals who lead active social lives are, almost by definition, healthier than their counterparts who rarely leave their homes or interact with others. So we can't really say whether being socially active prevents the onset of dementia, or if people who don't have dementia are more likely to be socially active.
paragraphs.translation: 其他关于成功老龄化的研究表明，与社区保持联系并拥有丰富的社交互动在延迟甚至预防痴呆症发作方面也很重要。然而，再次强调，结果远不如大众媒体可能让你相信的那么清晰。几乎根据定义，拥有活跃社交生活的老年人比很少离家或与他人互动的对应者更健康。所以我们不能真正说社交活跃是否能预防痴呆症的发作，还是没有痴呆症的人更可能社交活跃。

paragraphs.text: But even if studying a foreign language is not a magical cure-all, there is one thing it will do: It will make you a better speaker of a foreign language. Doing that confers a whole host of advantages we do know about.
paragraphs.translation: 但即使学习外语不是神奇的万能药，有一件事它会做到：它会让你成为更好的外语使用者。这样做会带来一系列我们确实知道的好处。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Research is meant to benefit society by raising public awareness and creating products and innovations that enhance development. For research to serve its full purpose, the results must leave the confines of research laboratories and academic journals.
paragraphs.translation: 研究旨在通过提高公众意识、创造促进发展的产品和创新来造福社会。要使研究充分实现其目的，研究结果必须走出研究实验室和学术期刊的局限。

paragraphs.text: Findings effectively communicated can go a long way to serve the interests of the public. They can help address social injustices or improve treatments offered to patients.
paragraphs.translation: 有效传达的研究成果可以大大服务于公众利益。它们可以帮助解决社会不公或改善为患者提供的治疗。

paragraphs.text: Many researchers seem to be content with sharing the results of their studies in academic journals or at conferences. But few journals allow everybody to read the findings. Even articles freely available are usually written in academic language incomprehensible to the average reader.
paragraphs.translation: 许多研究人员似乎满足于在学术期刊或会议上分享他们的研究成果。但很少有期刊允许所有人阅读这些发现。即使免费提供的文章通常也使用普通读者难以理解的学术语言写成。

paragraphs.text: For researchers in the tenure-track system, their main goal is winning tenure, which in part can be achieved by getting a number of papers published in prominent journals. Pressures like this mean community-level outreach is not prioritised.
paragraphs.translation: 对于处于终身教职轨道系统的研究人员来说，他们的主要目标是获得终身教职，这在一定程度上可以通过在知名期刊上发表一定数量的论文来实现。像这样的压力意味着社区层面的推广并不被优先考虑。

paragraphs.text: Many researchers lack the writing skills to describe their results to a general audience. They may also worry about whether the public will understand their findings, or about findings being used to influence controversial policies. These concerns cause some researchers to shy away from communicating their findings outside the academic community.
paragraphs.translation: 许多研究人员缺乏向普通读者描述其结果的写作技能。他们也可能担心公众是否会理解他们的发现，或者担心发现被用来影响有争议的政策。这些担忧导致一些研究人员避免在学术界之外交流他们的发现。

paragraphs.text: Propagating research findings beyond academic publications is particularly crucial for addressing certain social discrepancies. It can help families, communities, healthcare providers, policymakers, government agencies and other stakeholders to understand and respond to crises that plague society.
paragraphs.translation: 在学术出版物之外传播研究成果对于解决某些社会差异尤为关键。它可以帮助家庭、社区、医疗提供者、政策制定者、政府机构和其他利益相关者理解和应对困扰社会的危机。

paragraphs.text: The benefits of sharing findings flow both ways. Engaging with other researchers and the public can lead to unexpected new connections and new ideas that could suggest fruitful new directions for research.
paragraphs.translation: 分享研究成果的好处是双向的。与其他研究人员和公众互动可以带来意想不到的新联系和新想法，从而为研究指明富有成效的新方向。

paragraphs.text: To benefit both researchers and the communities, the need to find innovative, accessible ways to share the work cannot be overstated.
paragraphs.translation: 为了使研究人员和社区都受益，找到创新、易懂的方式来分享工作的必要性怎么强调都不为过。

paragraphs.text: Institutions and funding organisations should support more researchers to publish in open access journals so that the public doesn't have to pay to read them. Institutions and researchers should invest in partnerships that expand capacity for sharing results more broadly.
paragraphs.translation: 机构和资助组织应支持更多研究人员在开放获取期刊上发表论文，这样公众就不需要付费阅读。机构和研究人员应投资于合作伙伴关系，以扩大更广泛分享成果的能力。

paragraphs.text: Furthermore, ethics committees should make it mandatory for researchers to share their results with the public. Every research participant should opt in or out of receiving results, as part of the process of giving informed consent.
paragraphs.translation: 此外，伦理委员会应强制要求研究人员与公众分享他们的结果。作为给予知情同意过程的一部分，每个研究参与者都应选择是否接收结果。

paragraphs.text: There could be misunderstanding of the findings presented by the researcher because of technical terms. But this can be resolved by researchers engaging the services of professional writers or communication officers to help with translating their study into more accessible language and share it widely with media outlets and the public.
paragraphs.translation: 由于技术术语，研究人员呈现的发现可能会被误解。但这可以通过研究人员聘请专业作家或沟通官员的服务来解决，帮助将他们的研究翻译成更易懂的语言，并与媒体和公众广泛分享。

paragraphs.text: Sharing results with the people who are most affected by them makes us better researchers and ensures that our work can be used to improve people's lives. Institutions and collaborators must recognise the value of doing so.
paragraphs.translation: 与最受影响的人分享结果使我们成为更好的研究人员，并确保我们的工作可以用来改善人们的生活。机构和合作者必须认识到这样做的价值。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Spiders make their presence felt in late August and through early autumn. This is the mating season of some of the most common varieties, when male house spiders come out of hidden corners to look for females, and garden spiders reach adult size and spin their most dazzling webs.
paragraphs.translation: 蜘蛛的踪迹常在夏末秋初显现。此时正值某些常见蜘蛛的交配季节，雄性家蛛会从隐蔽角落爬出寻找雌蛛，园蛛也发育成熟并编织出最令人惊叹的蛛网。

paragraphs.text: Yet while the spider is a familiar fixture of nursery poems or songs and Halloween decorations, its relationship with humans is complicated. Fear of spiders is common and has serious impacts on the lives of sufferers. Its prevalence appears unrelated to any rational assessment of risk. Spiders in the UK are almost all harmless. Farmland species perform valuable ecosystem services, by preying on insects that are our competitors for crops. But they are a constant source of human anxieties—with a cultural association with witches and wickedness dating back to the middle ages.
paragraphs.translation: 然而，尽管蜘蛛是童谣和万圣节装饰中熟悉的元素，它们与人类的关系却颇为复杂。蜘蛛恐惧症相当普遍，对患者的生活影响严重。这种恐惧似乎与理性风险评估无关——英国的蜘蛛几乎全部无害。农田蜘蛛捕食与人类争夺农作物的昆虫，为生态系统提供重要服务。但它们始终是人类焦虑的源头，这种文化关联可追溯至中世纪与巫术和邪恶的联系。

paragraphs.text: Does this perhaps explain, in part, the lack of data about how spiders are faring in our age of ecological crisis? British butterflies are the most studied group of insects in the world, due to the long tradition of collecting and observing them. But spider conservationists point out that it was only in the 1980s that the classification of house spiders was properly sorted out. And while information about insect populations is gathered by experiments that measure the numbers hitting windscreens or traps, there have been few attempts to count spiders.
paragraphs.translation: 这是否能部分解释，在生态危机时代关于蜘蛛生存状况的数据如此匮乏？由于长期收集观察的传统，英国蝴蝶成为全球研究最深入的昆虫类群。但蜘蛛保护专家指出，直到20世纪80年代家蛛的分类才被彻底厘清。虽然可通过实验（如统计撞击挡风玻璃或落入陷阱的昆虫数量）收集昆虫种群信息，但针对蜘蛛的计数尝试却寥寥无几。

paragraphs.text: The huge reductions in the numbers of flying insects can only mean a reduction in spiders' food supply. A recent landmark study identified a 75% fall in insect populations between 1989 and 2016, with pesticide use thought to be to blame along with the destruction of wild areas for development. This means the overall picture for spiders is worrying, as it is for most creatures. But conservationists are most concerned about those varieties that are threatened due to habitat loss and fragmentation, which makes it impossible for them to migrate.
paragraphs.translation: 飞行昆虫数量的锐减必然导致蜘蛛食物供应减少。近期一项里程碑研究指出，1989至2016年间昆虫种群下降75%，原因除栖息地被开发破坏外，农药使用也被认为难辞其咎。这意味着蜘蛛的整体生存状况令人担忧，多数生物亦面临同样困境。但保护者最关注的是那些因栖息地丧失和碎片化而濒危的品种，这使得它们无法迁徙。

paragraphs.text: Of around 650 spider species regularly recorded in the UK, the majority thrive in marshes and wasteland. Conservation efforts, often led by determined individuals, have helped some species to recover by reintroducing them to new areas. With rewilding now firmly on the environmental policy agenda, the hope is that in future, spiders will be enabled to migrate by themselves, adapting to climate change by moving along wildlife corridors.
paragraphs.translation: 英国常规记录的约650种蜘蛛中，多数在沼泽和荒地繁衍生息。通过将个别物种重新引入新栖息地，常由个人主导的保护工作已帮助部分品种恢复数量。随着荒野重塑计划被明确纳入环境政策议程，未来有望通过建立生态廊道使蜘蛛自主迁徙，从而适应气候变化。

paragraphs.text: It seems unlikely that spiders will ever attract the same level of human enthusiasm as bees, birds or butterflies, in spite of their unique status as nature's spinners. But as they reveal themselves in all their splendour this autumn, it would be a good thing if more animal lovers recognised the ways in which spiders are simply terrific.
paragraphs.translation: 尽管蜘蛛拥有“自然纺纱工”的独特地位，它们恐怕永远无法像蜜蜂、鸟类或蝴蝶那样赢得人类同等的热情。但当这些生物在秋日尽展风采时，若能有更多动物爱好者认识到蜘蛛的非凡之处，将是一件美好的事情。

wrongOptions.A: 虽然文中提到蜘蛛在生态系统中的独特地位，但并未说作者希望人们因此而认识蜘蛛，属于过度推断。
wrongOptions.B: 文中没有提到希望人们对蜘蛛比对蝴蝶更热情，属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: 文中提到野生动物走廊对蜘蛛迁徙有帮助，但并未说作者希望有更多这样的走廊，属于过度推断。

questionGroups.sourceText: 近年来，中国老龄人口持续增长。中国政府正采取各种措施，推进养老服务体系建设，使老年人晚年生活健康幸福。全国兴建了各类养老服务机构。为了提升养老机构的服务质量，政府颁布了一系列标准，加强对养老机构的监管。许多城市为方便老年人用餐，开设了社区食堂，为他们提供价格实惠的饭菜。行动不便的老年人还能享受上门送餐服务。同时，中国还在积极探索居家和社区养老等其他养老模式，以确保所有老年人老有所养。

answer.modelTranslation: In recent years, the aging population in China has been growing continuously. The Chinese government is taking various measures to advance the construction of an elderly care service system, ensuring that the elderly lead a healthy and happy life in their later years. Various types of elderly care institutions have been established across the country. To enhance the quality of service in these institutions, the government has issued a series of standards and strengthened supervision over them. Many cities have opened community canteens to facilitate meal access for the elderly, providing them with affordable meals. Home delivery services are also available for those with mobility issues. Meanwhile, China is actively exploring other elderly care models such as home-based and community care, to ensure that all elderly people are well taken care of.
